newsitem.title: USA: Consumer spending, incomes up in March.
newsitem.headline: Consumer spending, incomes up in March.

text.p: Consumers steadily boosted their spending during March, the Commerce Department said on Thursday, encouraged by robust job growth that fattened incomes and kept savings accounts growing.

Spending increased by 0.5 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $5.37 trillion after an upwardly revised 0.5 percent gain in February. Incomes from wages, salaries and all other sources rose 0.6 percent to a rate of $6.75 trillion following a revised 0.8 percent February pickup.
The steady growth in spending and incomes reflected healthy economic conditions that generated higher incomes and spending throughout the first quarter and shows few signs of slackening.
Previously, the department said February incomes had risen by 0.9 percent and that spending had grown by 0.3 percent but it revised both estimates in the March report.

The Commerce Department reported on Wednesday that the national economy expanded at its fastest clip in nine years during the first quarter, with gross domestic product roaring ahead at a 5.6 percent annual rate in the three months from January through March.
Sharply higher consumer spending accounted for the lion's share of the first-quarter growth, the government said, which was further reflected in Thursday's report on incomes and spending.
Spending in March increased for all types of durable goods like new cars, for quickly used nondurables like food and paper products and for services from medical care to accountancy.
Even so, savings were higher becasue of stronger incomes.
The department said that 5.3 cents out of each dollar earned went into savings during March, up from 5.2 cents in February and 4.9 cents in January.

Private-sector wages and salaries increased by $25.3 billion in March after a $45.5 billion jump in February, the Commerce Department said. Exceptionally mild weather during February prompted a boom in construction activity.
There were 175,000 new jobs created in March, the government reported at the beginning of April, as a healthy economy bolstered consumer confidence and willingness to spend.
The Labour Department is scheduled to release employment figures for April on Friday amid expectations another 211,000 jobs were generated by the rising economic tide.

Gains in personal income, which includes not only wages and salaries but also income from sources such as dividends, interest and businesses, are essential for funding consumer purchases that fuel two-thirds of national economic activity.
Spending on durable goods, which includes cars, rose 0.7 percent to an annual rate of $664.4 billion in March from $660 billion in February.

Spending on nondurable products gained 0.4 percent to a rate of $1.61 trillion from $1.60 trillion in February while spending for services was up 0.5 percent to $3.10 trillion in March from $3.09 trillion.
Private-sector wages and salaries rose to an annual rate of $3.83 trillion during March from $3.80 trillion in February.
Payrolls of manufacturing companies rose to a $699 billion rate from $693 billion during February.
